:::{#exr-coordinate-vector-practice}
#### Describing a point on a plane in $\reals^3$ with two numbers

A point on a plane through the origin in $\reals^3$ needs only two numbers,
its [coordinate vector](#def-coordinate-vector) in a [basis](#def-basis) of the plane.
The vectors $\vecf{a}_1 = \tp{(1, 1, 0)}$ and $\vecf{a}_2 = \tp{(0, 1, 1)}$ form a basis of a plane $\mathcal{S}$,
which contains

$$
\vecf{x} = \sbmat{2 \\ 5 \\ 3}.
$$

Find the coordinate vector of $\vecf{x}$ in the basis $\vecf{a}_1, \vecf{a}_2$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Write $c_1 \vecf{a}_1 + c_2 \vecf{a}_2$ entry by entry,
then use @def-coordinate-vector.

:::

:::
